narrative.overview: The hub is the product taskcell.dev shows: the landing's near-black floor (#0d1013), cool ink, teal-tinted hairlines and one amber accent, in Schibsted Grotesk, Atkinson Hyperlegible and IBM Plex Mono. It stays a tool people check, so it takes the landing's palette and type but not its display sizes, glow or 3D scene. Dark is the default; light is derived. Amber marks the one main action per screen, focus, selection and live state, never decoration. Other color is status (green, yellow, red) or the project's identity color in the title bar.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black floor, cool ink, teal-tinted hairlines (landing palette).
One amber accent with dark ink on it, for action, focus and live state only.
One primary (filled) button per screen; everything else is outlined or text.
Hairline 1px borders and tonal steps instead of shadows; small, tight radii.
Landing faces, self-hosted: Schibsted Grotesk headings, Atkinson Hyperlegible text, IBM Plex Mono machine text.

rules.name: The Ink-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: A screen with nothing wrong and nothing running is ink, hairlines and one amber button. Status color appears only when its state is true.

rules.name: The One-Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber means act here or live. Not for decoration, headings or illustration; no Tailwind amber-* for new status.

rules.name: The Text-Shade Rule
rules.body: Colored text uses the *-text token, which keeps 4.5:1 in both themes (light overrides --success-text for the #f7f8f9 page). Never text-primary for text, text-green-600 dark:text-green-400 or text-rose-500.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change or be compared uses tabular-nums.

rules.name: The Machine-Text Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks text a machine produced or consumes. It is not a technical costume for headings, buttons or chat placeholders.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Separation is a 1px border-border line or a tonal step, not a shadow. A shadow means the thing floats above the page.

dos: Do import every visual primitive from `@/ui`; add a re-export there when a screen first needs a chunks-ui component.
Do use semantic tokens (`bg-success`, `text-destructive-text`, `border-border`) so both themes work; check new UI in light and dark.
Do keep one primary button per screen and put it at the right end of the page header row.
Do use the glossary words (Task, Run, Proof of Work, Stage, PR/MR) exactly.
Do give icon-only buttons an `aria-label` and every overlay dialog semantics.
Do use `tabular-nums` on numbers and monospace on ids, commands and code.
Do run the design detector over changed UI before committing (below).
donts: Don't use raw Tailwind palette colors (`text-green-600`, `bg-rose-500/5`) for status; only the board's column hues and sky info lines are allowed, and only where they already live.
Don't put a thick colored left border on cards, callouts or alerts (`border-l-4`).
Don't color a whole panel for a passed state; status color goes on the dot, chip or text.
Don't add display-size type, gradients, glass, the landing's glow or decorative illustration.
Don't add uppercase eyebrow labels above page headings.
Don't leak internal ticket refs (`(S6)`, `#491`) or the old `vanguard` name into UI copy.
